title: 8 Ways To Eliminate Parent Complaints Forever https://smartclassroommanagement.com/2009/09/26/8-ways-to-eliminate-parent-complaints-forever/
author: Michael Linsin
summary: Linsin argues that the best defense against parent complaints is proactive communication rather than a defensive reaction after the fact, since defending a teaching decision to an unhappy parent is a battle that damages reputation regardless of who is technically right. He offers eight specific tactics: sending a detailed parent information packet home covering the classroom management plan, homework policy, and restroom procedures, with a signed acknowledgment slip returned to school; reviewing the packet in person at back-to-school night; sending simple monthly progress reports; maintaining an open-door policy that welcomes parent visits; avoiding yelling, put-downs, or sarcasm; using a homework policy that doesn't require parental teaching; and, above all, ensuring students genuinely enjoy being in the class. He closes with a confident guarantee that following these steps will effectively 'complaint proof' a classroom.
points: Proactive, detailed communication with parents (packets, signed acknowledgments, progress reports) prevents most complaints before they start.
Reviewing expectations in person at back-to-school night closes the gap where parents feel blindsided by unexplained rules.
An open-door policy signals goodwill to parents even though few will actually take the teacher up on visiting.
A homework policy that doesn't require parental instruction avoids one of the most common sources of parent frustration.
Ultimately, students genuinely enjoying the classroom is described as the single best safeguard against parent complaints.
quotes: The best way to handle parent complaints is to listen politely, and then take action. Fix their problem, allay their fears, and do whatever you need to do in order to restore their confidence in you and your program.

Your reputation in your school community is critical and is never worth tarnishing, regardless of how “right” you may feel. Parents want you to do well, and it’s best to treat them like valued customers.
Send a parent information packet home the second week of school detailing your classroom management plan, homework policy, and restroom procedure. Most complaints come from these three.
It’s the teachers who prefer to teach behind closed doors who find themselves in the cross hairs of unhappy parents.
One of the keys to getting homework back each day is to assign only what students have proven they understand. Homework is between you and your students. Parents shouldn’t have to get involved.
Follow these eight strategies and you will effectively complaint proof your classroom. I guarantee it.
